title: graded-prioritizer-ttl-backoff-for-regional-throttle
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Introduces a graded request prioritizer with TTL-based backoff for regional request queues. Improves resilience against sudden regional traffic spikes by decaying priority over time and applying per-region token-bucket throttles. Includes observability and a canary rollout plan.
description:
Motivation: Recent incident analysis (SUP-3345) showed that sudden client-side retries can flood a single region's serving queue and exhaust capacity, causing cascading fallbacks and degraded p99 latency. This PR implements a graded priority decayer plus TTL-backed backoff that reduces the steady-state pressure from retry storms while preserving tail latency for high-priority requests.

What this change does: - Adds a GradedPrioritizer component that assigns a priority score to incoming requests based on route, token-tier, and recent success history. Priority decays over time using an exponential TTL decay window (configurable). - Implements a per-region token-bucket throttle that takes the graded priority into account; low-priority requests are admitted only if tokens are available or if they pass a fast-path for critical routes. - Adds a short-lived TTL backoff entry for detected retry loops: if a request is retried more than N times within M seconds, subsequent attempts get applied backoff weight for T seconds. - Wire up canary rollout policy (10% of traffic in region during first 1h, bump to 50% after checks) and automatic rollback on p95/p99 regressions. - Observability: metrics (region.prioritizer.admit_rate, region.prioritizer.drop_rate, region.prioritizer.ttl_entries, region.prioritizer.avg_priority), tracing tags, and two Grafana panels for quick health checks. - Tests: unit tests for the prioritizer and integration test that simulates retry storms with synthetic load.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4821) - [x] Unit tests for prioritizer and TTL decay - [x] Integration test validating canary behaviour - [x] Metrics and dashboards added - [x] Canary rollout config + automatic rollback threshold - [x] Docs: brief runbook update in reliability/README.md

High-level commits: - introduce graded prioritizer core loop and config - add per-region token-bucket throttle and admit/drop logic - TTL backoff store with expiry and metrics - integrate prioritizer into request router path - add tests and observability wiring - canary rollout manifests and config

Files touched (high level): pkg/serving/prioritizer.go, pkg/serving/prioritizer_test.go, pkg/serving/region_throttle.go, pkg/serving/ttl_backoff_store.go, internal/observability/metrics_register.go, deployments/canary/prioritizer-canary.yaml, docs/reliability/README.md, pkg/router/middleware.go, e2e/tests/retry_storm_sim.go

Why unique: This approach focuses on decaying priority over time (instead of immediate blackholing) and couples that decay with TTL backoff to reduce repeated pressure from retry loops while keeping high-priority traffic unaffected. The per-region token-bucket respects existing SLO allocations and integrates with our existing smart-routing fallbacks.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag prioritizer.enabled=false - Deploy canary manifest to one replica in us-west-2 with prioritizer.enabled=true at 10% traffic - Monitor metrics for 60 minutes; if region.prioritizer.drop_rate > 5% or p99 latency regresses by >10%, auto-rollback. - Gradually ramp to 50% and then 100% across regions after manual review.

Related: ENG-4987 (observability requirements), SUP-3345 (incident that motivated fix).
